summary: On reconnect, establish() overwrites clientRef.current with a brand-new GameClient but NEVER closes the previous one. Because the same onState closure is wired into every client and GameClient.handleClose() only self-suppresses when its own close() was called (this.closed), a stale client whose transport tears down LATE (e.g. server closed the control stream but kept the QUIC session, so wt.closed resolves seconds after readLoop already ended) will fire onState(false) AFTER the new client is live. That flips connectedRef=false, patches connected:false, and schedules yet another reconnect that spawns a THIRD client, orphaning the healthy one (leak + a duplicate stage session the server now sees).
scenario: Server closes only the bidi control stream (not the session). Old client's readLoop returns done -> onState(false) at t=0 -> reconnect at t=500ms -> new client connects, onState(true). At t~=1s the old session finally closes -> old wt.closed -> handleClose -> onState(false) (this.closed still false) -> connected flips to false on a live link and a spurious reconnect is scheduled, superseding and leaking the good client.
suggested_fix: Before assigning the new client, capture and close the old one: `const prev = clientRef.current; clientRef.current = client; void prev?.close();`. Alternatively neutralize the superseded client (null its handlers / mark it closed) so its late onState can't reach the shared handler.

summary: Same root defect as stage: on reconnect the old GameClient is only dropped by nulling clientRef.current (handleDisconnect line 265) and is never .close()d. handleDisconnect is a shared callback invoked by any client's onState(false). A stale client whose session closes AFTER a new client has connected will call handleDisconnect, which unconditionally stopHeartbeat()s the LIVE heartbeat, nulls the LIVE clientRef, and schedules another reconnect -> a second live socket for the same deviceFP/handle. Server-side dedup on deviceFP mitigates score loss, but you get connection churn / duplicate-connection anti-cheat flags and an orphaned leaked client.
scenario: Control stream closed but session lingers: old client onState(false) at drop -> reconnect -> new client connected & heartbeating -> old session closes late -> old wt.closed -> handleClose -> onState(false) -> shared handleDisconnect() tears down the live client and reconnects again.
suggested_fix: Close the old client in handleDisconnect (`const prev = clientRef.current; clientRef.current = null; void prev?.close();`) so GameClient.this.closed suppresses any late duplicate onState, and/or ignore onState from a client that is no longer clientRef.current.

summary: In establish(), only client.connect() is wrapped in try/catch. The subsequent `await client.send(hello)` / `await client.send(resync)` / startHeartbeat run unguarded. If the writable side rejects (transport half-broken) without the read side firing onState(false), the rejection escapes establish() (called via `void establish(...)`) as an unhandled promise rejection AND leaves clientRef.current set to a dead client with no heartbeat started and no reconnect scheduled — the scheduleReconnect guard `if (clientRef.current) return` and establish guard `if (clientRef.current) return` then both refuse to recover: a permanent wedge that only luck (a concurrent onState(false)) unsticks. This re-introduces exactly the unhandled-rejection class sweep-1 (uistage-5) hardened elsewhere with try/catch.
scenario: connect() resolves (onState(true) sets conn:connected), then the write stream errors before the read side surfaces onState(false). hello send rejects -> unhandled rejection; clientRef.current stays non-null with no heartbeat and no scheduled reconnect -> both reconnect guards short-circuit -> player stuck on 'live' with a dead socket.
suggested_fix: Wrap the post-connect hello/resync/startHeartbeat in try/catch that, on failure, nulls clientRef.current and calls scheduleReconnect() (mirroring the connect() catch).

summary: The grid renders `Array.from({ length: rows })` x `Array.from({ length: cols })` straight from server-supplied BoardData.rows/cols with no clamp. A malformed/corrupt board frame with a large rows*cols (e.g. 50000x50000) allocates billions of elements -> tab OOM/hang that the ErrorBoundary cannot catch (a synchronous hang, not a thrown error) — defeating the very 'malformed board frame must never freeze the projector' guarantee the sweep cited. The defensive `cells ?? []` handles a missing cells array but not absurd dimensions.
code:
{Array.from({ length: rows }).map((_, rIdx) => {
  return Array.from({ length: cols }).map((__, cIdx) => { ... }) })}
scenario: Server (or a corrupted frame) sends rows=50000, cols=50000. The render synchronously tries to build ~2.5e9 cells -> projector tab freezes/OOMs with no ErrorBoundary recovery.
suggested_fix: Clamp before rendering, e.g. `const r = Math.min(Math.max(rows|0,0), 12), c = Math.min(Math.max(cols|0,0), 12);` (or a sane MAX) and render from the clamped values.
